findings.title: Journey 6 'Video Streaming Fundamentals' shows 18 steps (with every step title triplicated) while all other journeys show 6 grouped logical steps — list card and detail page both wrong, inconsistent with siblings
reproSteps: GET /api/journeys -> journey 6 stepCount=18; journeys 7/8/9/10 stepCount=6

GET /api/journeys/6 -> 18 step rows but only 6 distinct titles (each of 6 logical steps has 3 rows). The other journeys collapse their 3-rows-per-step into 6 logical steps; journey 6's rows carry distinct stepNumbers 1..18 so the group-aware UI never collapses them.
Open /journeys: the 'Video Streaming Fundamentals' card renders '18 steps'; every other card renders '6 steps'.

Open /journey/6: header badge reads '18 steps'; the Learning Path syllabus renders 18 step cards where each title ('Introduction to Video Streaming', 'Understanding Video Codecs', ...) appears 3 times in a row.
Contrast /journey/7: badge '6 steps', 6 syllabus cards, 6 distinct titles (correct).
findings.expected: Journey 6 should present 6 logical steps consistently on both the list card and detail page (like every other journey), grouping its 3-rows-per-step; a learner should not see the same step title listed three times.
findings.actual: Journey 6 reports and renders 18 steps with each of its 6 titles repeated 3x; the list card ('18 steps') and detail badge ('18 steps') both disagree with the group-aware convention used by journeys 7-10 ('6 steps'). '8-10 hours' duration paired with '18 steps' also reads inconsistently vs siblings.

findings.title: Anonymous 'Refresh recommendations' button on /advanced fires an authenticated-only request and returns 401 (console error + network 4xx during a normal anon flow)
reproSteps: As an anonymous visitor open /advanced and activate the 'AI Recommendations' tab (aria-selected asserted).
The panel renders a 'Refresh recommendations' button (data-testid=button-generate-recommendations) that is enabled for anon.
Click it.
Network: GET /api/recommendations?limit=10&refresh=true -> 401 Unauthorized; browser console logs 'Failed to load resource: 401'.
Panel then flips to the error state: 'Recommendations couldn’t be refreshed — You need to be signed in to do that. Please sign in and try again.'
findings.expected: An anonymous user should not be shown an enabled control that fires an authenticated-only endpoint and 401s; the panel should gate behind sign-in (or hide/disable Refresh) rather than surfacing a 401 + console error on a normal click.
findings.actual: Anon click triggers a 401 on /api/recommendations and a console error, then shows a post-hoc 'You need to be signed in' error.
consoleErrors: Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 401 (Unauthorized) (GET /api/recommendations?limit=10&refresh=true)

findings.title: Anonymous /advanced Recommendations copy claims the visitor is signed in ('Using your account activity', 'your feedback shape these picks') with no sign-in prompt
reproSteps: As anonymous, open /advanced, activate 'AI Recommendations'.
Header reads 'Personalized Recommendations — Account preferences, learning activity, and your feedback shape these picks.'
Card reads 'Using your account activity' / 'Add learning preferences for more precise matches. Existing activity and feedback still shape your results.'
No sign-in prompt appears anywhere in the panel (mentionsSignIn=false).
Same misleading copy reproduced at mobile 375x667.
findings.expected: For a visitor with no account, the copy must not assert 'your account activity', 'your feedback', or 'saved preferences shape your results'; it should honestly say results are non-personalized and prompt sign-in.
findings.actual: Anon sees possessive/account-implying copy as if signed in, with no account and no sign-in CTA in the panel.

findings.title: Anonymous 'Choose learning preferences' link on Recommendations is a dead end — /settings#learning-preferences has no learning-preferences section for anon
reproSteps: As anonymous on /advanced Recommendations, note the 'Choose learning preferences' button links to /settings#learning-preferences.
Navigate to /settings#learning-preferences as anon.
The #learning-preferences section does NOT exist (sectionExists=false), page does not scroll (scrollY=0); anon Settings only shows 'Appearance' and a 'Sign in for more' card.
findings.expected: The recommendations CTA for anon should route to sign-in (or Settings should reveal/anchor the learning-preferences area behind a sign-in prompt), not to an anchor that is absent for the anonymous state.
findings.actual: Anon lands on /settings with no #learning-preferences target and no learning-preferences UI; the CTA leads nowhere useful.

findings.title: Anonymous Recommendations empty state instructs the visitor to 'update your preferences' — an action unavailable to anonymous users
reproSteps: As anonymous, open /advanced Recommendations tab.
Because no recommendations are generated for anon, the empty state 'No unseen recommendations right now' renders.
Its guidance reads 'Restore hidden items, update your preferences, or try again to look for new catalog matches.'
findings.expected: The empty-state guidance for an anonymous user should not tell them to restore hidden items / update preferences (both require an account); it should prompt sign-in.
findings.actual: Anon is told to perform account-only actions (restore hidden items, update preferences) with no sign-in path.

findings.title: Journey 6 detail syllabus lists each step title three times consecutively (18 near-identical cards) — confusing learning-path presentation
reproSteps: Open /journey/6.

In the 'Learning Path' section, count syllabus step headings: 18 h3 headings but only 6 distinct titles — 'Introduction to Video Streaming' appears 3 times in a row, then 'Understanding Video Codecs' 3 times, etc.
Compare /journey/7 where 6 headings map to 6 distinct titles.
findings.expected: Each logical step should appear once in the syllabus (its 1-3 constituent resource rows nested under a single step), as journeys 7-10 do.
findings.actual: Journey 6 renders each logical step as three separate, identically-titled step cards, so the learning path shows the same step title repeated three times consecutively.

findings.title: /code-of-conduct returns a 404 'Page Not Found' though it is enumerated as a public route in the surface map (route absent from router and sitemap)
reproSteps: Navigate to /code-of-conduct in the SPA.
Page renders 'Page Not Found' (title 'Page Not Found — Awesome Video') and the network shows a 404 for the route.
Reproduced twice via curl: HTTP 404 both times. Not present in the client router or sitemap.xml.
findings.expected: Either the /code-of-conduct page exists (it is listed as a public route) or it is not advertised as a public surface. A documented public route should not 404.
findings.actual: The documented public route /code-of-conduct 404s. (Note: no rendered UI link points to it — footer links only About/Terms/Privacy — so user impact is limited to typed/bookmarked/documented URLs.)
consoleErrors: Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (Not Found) (/code-of-conduct)

findings.title: Cross-surface login-link inconsistency: /submit uses '/sign-in?redirect_url=%2Fsubmit' while /journey/:id anon gate uses a bare setLocation('/login') (extra legacy redirect hop, no post-login return)
reproSteps: On /submit as anon, the 'Login required' banner links to /sign-in?redirect_url=%2Fsubmit (deep link with return URL).
On /journey/6 as anon, the 'log in' button calls setLocation('/login'), which is a LegacyAuthRedirect to /sign-in with NO redirect_url — after sign-in the user is not returned to the journey.
Clicked the journey 'log in' button: navigation lands on /sign-in (no redirect_url query).
findings.expected: Both anon gates should route to the same auth surface with a redirect_url back to the originating page, so a user returns to the journey/submit form after signing in.
findings.actual: The journey gate loses the return path (goes to /login -> /sign-in with no redirect_url), while /submit preserves it — an inconsistent, lossy login hand-off across two engagement surfaces.
